lead.headline: Democrats Win Control of Both Houses of Congress
lead.deck: After the midterm elections, Democrats will run the House and the Senate. Republicans are choosing new leaders.
body: Americans voted in midterm elections on Tuesday 3 November. Congress has two houses: the House of Representatives and the Senate. Democrats will control both when the new Congress meets in January.
In the House, Democrats had won at least 240 seats to the Republicans’ 147. In the Senate, the Democratic group will have at least 54 senators. Alaska and Mississippi were too close to call.

The loss is changing who leads Republicans. House Speaker Mike Johnson said he will not try to lead House Republicans in the next Congress. Two Republican representatives, Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan, both said they will run for minority leader. Democrat Hakeem Jeffries will run for speaker, and he would be the first African American to hold that job.

world.headline: Oil Prices Drop More Than 8% in One Day
world.deck: Hopes for an end to the Iran war pushed oil to its lowest price since 31 August.
body: The price of crude oil fell by more than 8% on Wednesday 4 November. Oil is made into fuel for cars, trucks and planes.
Brent crude, a widely used world price, fell $8.98 to $94.62 a barrel. A second price, called WTI, fell $7.97 to $88.12. Both were the lowest finishing prices since 31 August.
Traders hoped the war between Iran and the United States and Israel might end. Shares of energy companies fell 4.8% as oil got cheaper.
